text: From the following common size statement percentages, which one represents the percentage of net sales to total assets?
explanation: Common size statement percentages are calculated by expressing each item of the financial statement as a percentage of a base item. In this case, the percentage of net sales to total assets is calculated by dividing net sales by total assets and multiplying by 100.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the purpose of comparative financial statements?
options: To compare the financial position of two companies
To compare the financial position of a company over a period of time
To compare the financial position of a company with its competitors
To compare the financial position of a company with its industry
correctAnswer: To compare the financial position of a company over a period of time
explanation: Comparative financial statements are used to compare the financial position of a company over a period of time. This helps to identify trends and changes in the company's financial position.
subject: Accountancy

text: What is the formula for calculating the percentage of net profit to net sales?
options: ($Net Profit ÷ Net Sales) × 100
($Net Sales ÷ Net Profit) × 100
($Net Profit ÷ Total Assets) × 100
($Total Assets ÷ Net Profit) × 100
explanation: The percentage of net profit to net sales is calculated by dividing net profit by net sales and multiplying by 100.
